title: Best Hair Clippers UK
short: Hair clippers compared by battery life, cutting range and build quality, from budget corded models to professional-grade clippers.
intro: A good set of clippers can save a monthly trip to the barber, and the difference between models comes down to motor power, cutting range and how long a cordless model lasts between charges. This guide compares clippers tested by Expert Reviews, from budget corded picks to a genuine professional-grade model.

guide.a: Mains-powered clippers give consistent full power throughout use, which some find better for thick or unruly hair, and they never run out of charge mid-cut. Cordless models are easier to manoeuvre single-handed if cutting your own hair and are more portable for travel, though they typically cost more for similar quality.

Grades indicate how short the clipper cuts using comb attachments: grade 1 is roughly 3mm and grade 8 is around 25mm. Most clippers, like those in this guide, come with a comb set spanning grades 1-8, plus tapered combs for neatly trimming around the ears.

guide.q: How much should I spend on clippers?
guide.a: Most clippers sell for under £50 and can give a good or excellent cut depending on skill, while professional barbers typically pay £100 or more, like the Oster 606 here. As a rule, expect the difference in price to buy stronger motors, sharper blades and better durability rather than a fundamentally different cutting result for occasional home use.

guide.q: How long does cordless battery life need to be?
guide.a: For a single haircut, 20-30 minutes of runtime is usually enough, but models with 60-120 minutes like those in this guide give more headroom for beard trims too or if you're cutting more than one person's hair. Also check charging time, since some budget cordless models take up to 12 hours to fully charge.
